questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** i - b, ii - a, iii - c, iv - d**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **cell **physically expands, duplicates **organelles**, and creates the **molecular** building blocks it will require in subsequent **stages **during** G1phase**, also known as the** first gap phase**.
 
• The **cell **creates a full copy of the **DNA **in its nucleus during the **S phase**. Moreover, it makes duplicates of the **centrosome**, a structure that organises **microtubules**. During **M phase**, the **centrosomes **aid in the separation of **DNA**.
 
• The second **gap** phase, also known as the **G2 phase**, is a time of increased cell **growth**, **protein** and **organelle **production, and content reorganisation in preparation for mitosis.
 
• The cell's nuclear **DNA **condenses into its visible chromosomes during mitosis and is separated by the mitotic spindle, a specialised microtubule-based structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Stages of the cell cycle**

 
 
• **​**A cell must grow, replicate its genetic material **(DNA)**, and physically split into two **daughter** cells before it may **divide**.
 
• The **cell cycle **is a structured, predictable series of actions that cells take to complete these **goals**.
 
• Because the two **daughter **cells can restart the entire **process **from the beginning after each **cycle**, the cell cycle is a **cycle** rather than a **linear pathway**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/20b251078149172c1b03f7d779402e459bab2398e8560645f0902597c44ed91d.png]

questions.question: If Q = net charge, t = time, then which of the following equations is correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **I =Q over t**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Current, charge and time**

 
 
• How much electric charge is transferred each second defines electrical current, giving the following relationship:

 **Current= charge/ time**

 Rearranging this we get,

 charge= current * time
 
• The symbol for charge is **Q**, it is measured in **coulombs (C).**
 
• The symbol for current is** I**, it is measured in **amperes (A).**
 
• The symbol for time is** t**, it is measured in **seconds (t).**
 
• This gives the relation:

 **Q= I* t**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Current**

 
 
• A stream of charged particles, like **electrons or ions**, moving through an electrical conductor or space is called an electric current.
 
• The net rate of electric **charge flow** through a surface or into a control volume is how it is measured.
 
• Depending on the conductor, the **moving particles** are referred to as charge carriers, which can be any one of a number of different types of particles.
 
 
 
• **Charge**
 
 
• A charge in physics can be any of a number of different quantities, such as the color charge in **quantum** chromodynamics or the electric charge in **electromagnetism.**
 
• The time-invariant generators of a symmetry group, and more specifically, the generators that commute with the **Hamiltonian**, are represented by charges.
 
• The charge invariance corresponds to the vanishing commutator **[Q,H]=0**, where H is the Hamiltonian because **charges** are frequently denoted by the letter Q.
 
• As a result, charges and **conserved quantum** numbers are linked; these are the **eigenvalues q **of the generator Q.
 
 
 
• **Time**
 
 
• From the past through the present and into the future, time is the ongoing sequence of existence and events that appears to be** irreversible.**
 
• It is a component quantity of various measurements used to order events, compare their **durations or intervals**, and quantify rates of change of quantities in material reality or conscious experience.
 
• Along with the three spatial dimensions, time is frequently referred to as a **fourth dimension.**

questions.question: With which instrument do the sisters Lalita and Nandini identify?

__
 
• ** Lalita and Nandini**

 
 
• **​**Globally renowned violin maestros** Dr. M. LALITHA and M. NANDINI** have been hailed as the current generation's **"QUEENS OF VIOLIN - Weekend."**
 
• Popularly referred to as the "Viola Sisters," these exceptional musicians have mesmerised audiences with their captivating music and have earned recognition as the** "ONLY FEMALE DUO IN ASIA to perform the World music, South Indian Classical, Fusion, and Western Classical music - Le Mauricien."**
 
• **"Music runs in their blood, they must have played music even while they were in their mother's womb," **said famous music critic Subbudu. Lalitha and Nandini are the torchbearers of a special musical history, but they have also developed their own unique styles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **mandolin **is a stringed instrument from the same family as the lute that is often played with a pick.
 
• Although there are also variations with** 4 string, 5 string, 6 string, 5 double string (10 strings), 6 (12 strings)**, and even **4 triple string (12 strings)** courses, the most typical configuration has four courses of doubled strings tuned in unison, providing a total of **8 strings**.
 
• A **stringed **instrument known as the sarod is utilised in **Hindustani **music on the Indian subcontinent. It is one of the most well-known and renowned instruments, along with the sitar. It is renowned for having a rich, substantial, inward tone.
 
• The **woodwind **family of instruments, which includes the **flute**, is used in** classical music**. Flutes are aerophones, which means they produce music by vibrating a column of **air**, like all woodwind instruments do.

questions.question: Guru Nileshwar Mukharjee is the exponent of which of the following Indian classical dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Manipuri__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• Guru Nileshwar Mukharjee

 
 
• ​Guru Nileshwar Mukharjee is a well-known Manipuri dancer from India who has achieved international fame.
 
• The Manipuri community is well aware of Guru Nileshwar Mukharjee, who has made significant contributions to the field of Manipuri dance. Guru Nileshwar Mukharjee gave a Ras performance in Sylhet in 1920, and Rabindranath Tagore was so moved that he summoned him to Shantiniketan.
 
• In the history of Manipuri dance, this event marked a turning point. Within a decade, it had transcended national boundaries and made Guru Nileshwar Mukharjee's name well-known around the world.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• Manipuri Dance

 
 
• One of the eight principal Indian classical dance styles, the Manipuri Dance is also known as the Manipuri Raas Leela (Meitei: Jagoi Raas, Raas Jagoi) and is a product of the state of Manipur.
 
• The dancing style is characterised by delicate, calm body motions and compassionate gaze, and it is infused with the spiritual themes of Madhura Raas of Radha-Krishna.
 
• Whether a dancer is Hindu or not, their expressions are generally calm and convey Bhakti Rasa, or the emotion of devotion.

questions.question: In which Five-Year Plan, was the Mahalanobis Model started?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Second**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahalanobis Model**

 
 
• **​Marxist **economists **Grigory** **Feldman** from the Soviet Union and **Prasanta** **Chandra** **Mahalanobis** from India separately developed the **Feldman-Mahalanobis model in 1953**.
 
• **Mahalanobis **ended up serving as the **Second Five Year Plan's** primary economist and was the focus of many of the country's most contentious economic discussions.
 
• The **core **of the **strategy** is a change in** industrial investmen**t patterns towards the development of a domestic **consumption goods sector.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Long-term expansion** of the nation's consumer** goods production** capacity depends on the capital goods sector having a high adequate capacity.
 
• The division between the two different categories of **goods **helped consumers better comprehend the **trade-off** between levels of immediate and** future consumption** and provided a clearer **explanation **of **Marx's **theories in** Das Kapital**.
 
• **Feldman**, an economist for the **GOSPLAN **planning committee at the time, first proposed these concepts in 1928, outlining the theoretical justifications for a** two-department growth strategy**.

questions.question: The Basketball centre line is part of the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Back Court**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Basketball**

 
 
• **​Basketball **is a team sport in which **two teams**, usually each with** five players**, compete against one another on a **rectangular **court with the main goal of **preventing** the **opposing** team.
 
• From shooting through their own hoop while putting the ball through the defender's hoop, which is a basket with a diameter of 18 inches (46 cm) mounted** 10 feet (3.048 m)** high to a **backboard** at each end of the court. 
 
• Timed play is stopped following a foul, and the player who committed the **foul **or who was chosen to attempt a **technical** foul is awarded one, two, or three **one-point free throws**.
 
• The team with the most points at the **conclusion **of regulation play **wins**, but if the score is tied when regulation play **ends**, extra time (overtime) must be **played**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Players **move the ball forward by either passing it to a **teammate** or **bouncing** it while running or walking (dribbling), both of which require a** high level** **of ability**.
 
• Players can use a variety of shots on offence, **such as layups, jump shots, and dunks**. On **defence**, they can steal the ball from a player who is **dribbling**,** intercept passes**, or** block shot**s.
 
• Finally, either the offence or the **defence** can grab rebounds, which are **missed shots** that **rebound off** the** rim** or **backboard**.

questions.question: From the point of view of commerce, the busiest ocean of the world is ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Atlantic Ocean**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Atlantic Ocean**

 
 
• **​**At a size of roughly** 106,460,000 km2**, the **Atlantic Ocean** is the **second-largest** of the world's five oceans **(41,100,000 sq m**i).
 
• It covers around** 29%** of the** sea surface area** and about **20%** of the **planet's surface**.
 
• The** "Old World" of Africa**, **Europe**, and **Asia** is known to be distinguished from the** "New World"** of the Americas in the perspective of **Europe**.
 
• The** Atlantic Ocean** has been crucial to the growth of **human society**, **globalisation**, and the history of numerous states since it divides **Africa**, **Europe**, and **Asia **from the **Americas**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Atlantic Ocean **served as the **epicentre** of the **Columbian **Exchange and the namesake slave trade from the **16th **through the **19th centuries**, and it also periodically served as the scene of **naval conflicts**.
 
• While there haven't been any major** military conflicts** in the **Atlantic **in the current **21st century**, the ocean still plays an important role in** international trade**.
 
• Both these naval battles and growing trade from** regional American powers** like the **United States and Brazil** increased in intensity during the **20th century.**
 
• The **Atlantic Ocean** is located in an elongated, **S-shaped basi**n that runs between **North** and **South America** to the **west** and **Europe** and **Africa** to the **east**.

questions.question: On which river, the first night navigation mobile application in rivers in India was launched for ferries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmaputra.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brahmaputra**

 
 
• **​**The **Brahmaputra **is a** trans-boundary** river that passes through **Tibet**, **Bangladesh**, and **Northeastern India**.
 
• Other names for it include **Luit **in **Assamese**, the **Yarlung Tsangpo** in **Tibetan**, the **Siang/Dihang River** in **Arunachali**, and the** Jamuna Rive**r in **Bangla**.
 
• It is the **15th **longest river in the world and the **9th **largest by discharge.
 
• The** Yarlung Tsangpo River** has its source in the** Manasarovar Lak**e region, close to **Mount Kailash**, in **Burang County**, **Tibet**, on the **northern **face of the **Himalayas**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **river **travels through southern Tibet before **plunging **into the **Mountains **in the **Yarlung Tsangpo** Great **Canyon **and entering **Arunachal Pradesh**.
 
• It enters **India** close to the** Arunachal Pradesh** settlement of Gelling and travels through **Bangladesh **as the **Jamuna** before flowing southwest through the** Assam Valley** (not to be confused with the **Yamuna **of India).
 
• It combines with the **Ganges**, also known as the **Padma** in **Bangladesh**, in the enormous **Ganges Delta**, where it then becomes the **Meghna** and eventually empties into the **Bay of Bengal**.

questions.question: Minhaj-i-Siraj was a chronicler during the rule of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sultan Iltutmish **__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Minhaj-i-Siraj **

 
 
• **​Minhaj-al-Din Siraj-al-Din Abu Amr Othman ibn Minhaj al-Siraj Juzjani**, also known as **Muhammad **Juzjani (born 1193), was a Persian historian who lived in the 13th century.
 
• He was born in the **Ghur district**. Juzjani moved to Ucch and then to Delhi in 1227.
 
• The main historian for the** Mamluk Sultanate of Delhi **in northern India was Juzjani. and discussed the Ghurid dynasty.
 
• Also, he penned the Tabaqat-i Nasiri (1260 CE) for Delhi's **Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah**. After 1266, he passed away.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Sultan Iltutmish **

 
 
• **​**The third **Mamluk king** to oversee the erstwhile **Ghurid lands in northern India** was Shams ud-Din Iltutmish.
 
• He is regarded as the de facto **founder of the Delhi Sultanate** because he was the first Muslim ruler to do so from Delhi.
 
• **Iltutmish **was sold into slavery as a young child and spent his early years in **Bukhara and Ghazni** working for many owners.
 
 

7d

questions.question: Joint Liability Group is usually an informal group that consists of ________ individuals who seek loans against mutual guarantee.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4-10**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Joint Liability Group**

 
 
• The **National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)**, a rural development organisation in India.
 
• It has developed the idea of Joint Liability Groups in 2014 to offer institutional finance to small farmers.
 
• In order to obtain a **loan **from a bank without providing any **collateral**, a Joint **Liability** Group is made up of four to ten individuals from the same **town** or **locality **who share a similar **socioeconomic** background.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **JLGs **can be promoted by Business Facilitators/Correspondents, **NGOs**, **Farmers Clubs**,** Farmers Federations**, **Panchayati Raj Institutions**, **Agricultural **Universities, **Bank Branches**, **PACS**, **Cooperative Societies**, **Individuals**, **mFIs**, and Many **Others**.
 
• A **bank **may choose to provide funding to a **JLG **either directly to the group or to an individual **member**. In either **scenario**, the **loan **balance must be repaid in full by all** JLG members**.

questions.question: Which of the following can alter the boundary of a state or change its name?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parliament**

 
 
• **​**The** Republic of India's** highest legislative body is the **Indian Parliament**.
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** (Council of States) and the** Lok Sabha** are the** two houses **that make up India's bicameral** legislature** (House of the People).
 
• The **president** has full authority to call a session of either **house of Parliament**, prorogue it, or dissolve the **Lok Sabha** in his capacity as head of the **legislature**.
 
• Only on the advice of the **prime minister** and his** Union Council of Ministers** can the **president** utilise these **powers**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **members **of the **Rajya Sabha** are chosen by the **members **of all **state legislative** assemblies via proportional **representation**, whereas the **members **of the** Lok Sabha** are chosen by the** Indian population **directly through voting in** single-member districts**.
 
• The authorised **membership **of the **Parliament** is **543 **in the **Lok Sabha** and **245** in the **Rajya Sabha**, including **12 candidates** with experience in a variety of **literary**, **artistic**, **scientific**, and **social service disciplines**. In New Delhi's** Sansad Bhava**n, the **Parliament **convenes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The **Vangas, Mauryans, and Guptas** were only a few of the ancient** pan-Indian dynasties** that ruled over this area.

questions.question: ________ is a change of position.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Motion is the process of moving or being moved, as well as a change in the position of an item.**
 
• The term "**body in motion**" refers to when a body's location in relation to its **environment changes.**
 
• **Motion** is mathematically characterised in terms of **displacement, distance, velocity, acceleration, and speed** as well as the observer's frame of reference and the measurement of the change in the body's position with respect to that frame as time passes.
 
• **Kinematics** is the field of physics that studies forces and their effects on motion, while **dynamics** studies the motion of objects without regard to their source.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speed**

 
 
• The distance travelled in relation to the time it took to travel that **distance** is how speed is defined. As **speed** simply has a direction and no **magnitude**, it is a **scalar** **quantity**.
 
 
 
• **Velocity**
 
 
• In **kinematics**, the area of classical mechanics that deals with the **motion** of bodies, **velocity** is a fundamental idea.** A physical vector quantity called velocity **must have both a **magnitude** and a direction in order to be defined.
 
 
 
• **Distance**
 
 
• **Distance** is the scientific term used to describe how far an object has moved. **A scalar quantity, distance.** **The International System of Units defines a metre as the distance unit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Muslim League** was established on** December 30, 1906, at Dacca**, under the direction of **Aga Khan**, the **Nawab of Dhaka,** and **Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk.**
 
• When **British India** was divided in 1947, a political party was the driving force behind the movement asking for the creation of a separate** Muslim nation** out of concern that **Hindus** would take over **an independent India.**
 
• It was established to protect** Indian Muslims' rights.**
 
• In** 1913, Muhammad Ali Jinnah** joined the league.
 
• The league was terminated on August 14th, 1947. In** Pakistan, Bangladesh, and India**, it is still present in political parties under different guises.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **The objectives of the league were:**

 
• To inspire loyalty to the** British government **among **Muslims**.
 
• To protect **Muslims' political rights** and to express such rights to the **government**.
 
• To combat the animosity **Muslims** have towards other **communities**.

questions.question: Chittaranjan Das was the political guru of which of the following personalities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Subhash Chandra Bose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On January 23, 1897, **Subhash Chandra Bose** was born in** Cuttack, Orissa Division, Bengal Province**.
 
• The 23rd of January is observed as "**Parakram Diwas**," the anniversary of** Netaji's **birth.
 
• **Subhash Chandra Bose** is more commonly referred to as "**Netaji**."
 
• **Vivekananda's** teachings had a significant impact on him, and he regarded him as his spiritual teacher.
 
• The "**Political Guru of Subhash Chandra Bose**" was** Chittaranjan Das.**
 
• At the **Tripuri Session in 1939** and the **Haripura Session in 1938, **he was the first** INC President **to be elected.
 
• In 1939, he created the **Forward Bloc**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chittaranjan Das**

 
 
• **​Chittaranjan Das**, also known as **Deshbandhu** (Friend of the Nation), was an **Indian freedom fighter**, political activist, and lawyer during the **Indian Independence Movement.**
 
• He also founded and served as the **leader of the Swaraj Party** in undivided Bengal during the time of **British Colonial rule in India. Chittaranjan Das** passed away on June 16, 1925.
 
• He goes by the initials** C. R. Das**. In addition to several articles and essays, he was closely affiliated with a number of literary clubs and composed poetry.

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs of ‘Dynasty-Ruled region’ is correctly matched?

I. Shakas - Northwest and north India

II. Vakatakas - Central and western India
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shakas** were of** Scythian ethnic descent**. With the **Great Yueh Chi tribe's (Chinese Tribe's)** expulsion of the **Shakas** from the plains of **Syr Darya (Jaxartes) **in the second century** BCE**, the **Shakas** moved into **northwest India.** Aspirants should be aware that the terms "**Sakas**," "**Shakas**," and "**Indo-Scythians"** are interchangeable and have the same meaning.
 
• In the middle of the third century **CE, the Deccan** was the place of genesis of the** ancient Indian dynasty known as the Vakataka.**
 
• Their **territory** is thought to have spanned the **Tungabhadra River in the south**, the **Arabian Sea in the west,** and the easternmost reaches of** Chhattisgarh**, as well as the southernmost reaches of **Malwa and Gujarat in the north**.
 
• They were the most significant **Satavahana successors in the Deccan **and lived at the same time as the **Guptas in northern India.** 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__
 
• **Shishunaga Dynasty**
 
 
• **Shishunaga Dynasty**, established in **Magadha by Shishunaga, an Amatya,** overthrew the **Haryanka Dynasty**.
 
• He organised the populace's uprising against the **Haryanka Dynasty**, conquered Magadha, and established **Patliputra** as its capital.
 
• The son of a** Licchavi king of Vaishali was Shishunaga**. In addition to **Sindh, Karachi, Lahore, Herat, Multan, Kandahar, and Vellore, Shishunaga** extended his realm to include modern-day **Jaipur in Rajasthan.**
 
• Even the **Shishunaga Dynasty** expanded to **Madurai and Cochin** in the south, **Murshidabad** in the east, and Mand in the west. **Kakavarna**, also known as **Kalashoka**, and his ten sons succeeded **Shishunaga**.
 
• The throne of this nation was afterwards taken by the **Nanda Empire.**

questions.question: Who was appointed as India's chief G20 coordinator in April 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harsh V Shringla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harsh Vardhan Shringla**, who was born in 1962, will serve as **India's chief coordinator for the G20 in 2023.**
 
• Prior to this, he held positions as **Thailand's ambassador,** **Bangladesh's high commissioner, **and** India's foreign secretary.**
 
• **Harsh Vardhan Shringla** attended **Mayo College in Ajmer** before earning his degree from **St. Stephen's College at Delhi University.**
 
• Prior to joining the** Indian Foreign Service**, he worked in both the public and commercial sectors of India. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **G20**

 
 
• The **Group of Twenty, or G20**, is an** intergovernmental organisation** made up of the **European Union and 19 other nations (EU).**
 
• It strives to address important global economic concerns like **international financial stability**, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and **sustainable development.**
 
• The majority of the world's greatest economies, both industrialised and developing countries, make up the **G20**; together, they represent two-thirds of the world's population, **60% **of its land area, and around **80%** of the** world's gross world product (GWP).**

questions.question: The Purple revolution was launched by the Union Ministry of Science & Technology in Jammu and Kashmir. This revolution is related to cultivation of which crop?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lavender**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• With the **Council of Scientific and Industrial Research's "aroma mission," the Ministry of Science and Technology's Purple Revolution or Lavender Revolution **seeks to advance the domestic aromatic **crop-based agro-economy (CSIR)**.
 
• The goal aims to boost farmers' incomes and encourage large-scale commercial **lavender farming.**
 
• The major product is lavender oil, which goes for at least **Rs. 10,000 per litre.**
 
• Medicines, incense sticks, soaps, and air fresheners are some more popular goods.
 
• **Lavender** growing is particularly cost-effective because it generates income right away.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• By switching from imported aromatics to domestic ones, it seeks to advance the **domestic** **aromatic crop-based agro-economy.**
 
• The objective included providing free **lavender seedlings **to first-time growers, and paying those who had previously grown** lavender Rs. 5–6 per plant.**
 
• **Lavender** growing has started in the** Ramban district of Jammu and Kashmir** as part of the **CSIR-Aroma Indian Institute of Integrative Medicine (IIIM) Programme.**
 
• Almost all **20 districts of Jammu and Kashmir have lavender farms. **

questions.question: The atomic number of lead is ___________.
questions.solution:

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deals with amendment in the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 368**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part XX (Article 368)** of the** Indian Constitution **outlines the** constitutional amendment process.**
 
• This process protects the** Constitution of India's** sanctity and serves as a check on the arbitrary authority of the **Indian Parliament**.
 
• **Article 368** does not clearly forth the **legislative process** to be followed at various points of the change.
 
• **The Indian Constitution's Article 368 **deals directly with** constitutional amendments. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 365**

 
 
• ​According to **Article 365**, the **President** may declare that a situation has arisen in which the **State's government** cannot be carried out in accordance with the provisions of this **Constitution** if any State has failed to comply with or give effect to any directives provided in the exercise of the Union's executive power under any of the provisions of this **Constitution**.
 
 
 
• **Article 360**
 
 
• The **Indian Constitution's Part XVIII (Articles 352-360) **discusses the **Emergency Provisions. Article 360** specifically addresses the current financial crisis. The **Indian Constitution** contains three different categories of emergency provisions. The remaining two are:
 
 
• **National Emergency - Article 352**
 
• Emergency resulting from a breakdown of the state's constitutional machinery - **President's Rule - Article 356**
 
 
 
 
 
• **Article 355**
 
 
• "It shall be the duty of the Union to defend every State from external invasion and internal unrest and to ensure that the **government** of every State is carried on in conformity with the provisions of this **Constitution**," states **Article 355 of the Constitution.**

questions.question: By which name is the historical road built by Sher Shah Suri known?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Grand trunk road**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sher Shah Suri**, a king of the **16th century**, constructed the **Grand Trunk Road**.
 
• It was referred to as "**Sadak e Azam**."
 
• The road was essential for inland trade since it connected **India to Central Asia.**
 
• This street's previous names include **Uttarapath, Badshahi Sarak, and Sarak e Azam**.
 
• The longest and oldest significant road in Asia.
 
• **3,710 kilometers **make up this road's length.
 
• The west end of this route is in** Kabul, Afghanistan**, and the east end is in **Teknaf, Bangladesh**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sher Shah Suri**

 
 
• **Sher Shah Suri (1472, or 1486 - 22 May 1545)**, born **Farid Khan,** was the founder of the **Sur Empire in India**, with its capital in** Sasaram** in modern-day **Bihar**.
 
• He reduced the weight of silver coins to 178 grams and gave the money the Sanskrit name rupee, which is an ancient synonym for silver.
 
• In the year** 1540 CE, Sher Shah **seized power over the** Mughal Empire**. His son** Islam Shah** succeeded him after his untimely death in** 1545 CE. **

questions.question: The poverty ratio declined to ________ in 2011-12 in rural India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30**____**.9%**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the "Rangarajan Report on Poverty", **the poverty ratio has declined from 39.6% in 2009-10 to 30.9% in 2011-12 in rural India**__ and from 35.1% to 26.4% in urban India.
 
• The all-India ratio was 29.5%. In rural India, 260.5 million individuals were below poverty and in urban India 102.5 million were under poverty. Totally, 363 million were below poverty in 2011-12.
 
• 
 
 The Methodology recommended by the Expert Group (Rangarajan) for estimation of poverty is as follows:

 __
 
• 
 
The poverty line should be based on certain normative levels of adequate nourishment, clothing, house rent, conveyance and education, and a behaviorally determined level of other non-food expenses.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Poverty **

 
 
• When a person lacks the means of support and necessities for a given level of living, they are said to be in a state or condition of poverty.
 
• Several social, economic, and political factors can contribute to or be a result of poverty.
 
• There are two major ways to assess poverty in statistics and economics: absolute poverty compares income to the amount required to cover basic requirements like food, clothes, and shelter; relative poverty assesses how well a person is doing in comparison to others in the same situation.

questions.question: In a lake ecosystem, the primary consumers are ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**zooplankton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Although there may be some fish that consume **phytoplanktons**, the main consumers in a** lake environment are zooplanktons. Zooplankton** is thus the dominant second **trophic level** in a **lake environment.**
 
• The majority of **zooplankton** **species** are tiny, microscopic organisms. a single-celled protist that primarily consumes **bacteria**, for instance. Nonetheless, some **zooplankton** species can grow fairly large such as jellyfish, arrow worms, etc.
 
• They are the main consumers because they consume producers like **phytoplankton**, which are then consumed by small fish **(secondary consumers).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Food Chain**

 
 
• **A food chain **demonstrates the relationship of feeding between several creatures in a** specific habitat or ecosystem.**
 
• The energy flow from the **sun to producers,** from** producers to consumers,** and from **consumers to** **decomposers** like** fungi is demonstrated by a food chain.**
 
• They also **demonstrate** how animals rely on other living things for nourishment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bfb028831fa5e71350035ea92fc9fcd594cc370f7b30f7977da5346cb9fd9b3f.png]
